p1_every_role_validated.was: `_job_eligibility` derived compatibility and exclusions only when stage.kind == 'implementation'. Review and integration got an empty exclusion list after one Work comparison, so job-b/review on Work B reserved the review worker whose manifest names Work A; `single_worker` refused it correctly but only AFTER the reservation, leaving RESERVED capacity and no admit receipt.
p1_every_role_validated.now: `_job_workers(deployment, stage, job)` derives the servable workers for EVERY role by one rule, and `_disagreements` reads `single_worker._matches`'s own six operands from the worker's held deployment rather than restating them: launch role, the manifest's Work, the workload profile name and digest, the manifest digest against the Job's submitted input, and the policy digest. `_job_eligibility` excludes every configured worker outside that set, so only a Job-compatible worker is reservable. A stage with NO compatible worker is refused before reserve, naming each lane worker's disagreements.
p1_every_role_validated.still_bound_by_identity: the implementation kind is additionally held to the binding's `source_worker_id`: another worker agreeing on every digest is still some other Job's source
p1_every_role_validated.integration_scoped_to_the_configured_act: the integration kind is additionally held to the deployment's own `integration_profile.integrator_participant`, because the profile, the delivery and all four receipt sessions belong to that actor. This constrains eligibility to an actor already configured; it grants no second integrator and no new profile or driver capability.

p1_reconstruction.was: `_allocation` consults the independence callback ONLY when it creates a reservation, so an allocation recorded before this deployment bound the Job was used on every later tick with nothing re-deriving whether that worker still serves it.
p1_reconstruction.now: `StageExecution.admit` is spelled here -- it was reaching the pooled surface by delegation -- and revalidates a RECORDED allocation's worker against the same `_job_workers` rule before delegating. It reserves nothing, releases nothing and adds no scheduler operation; it refuses to admit against an allocation that cannot serve the Job.
p1_reconstruction.signature: admit(stage, job=None); the manager calls admit(stage, job) and the pooled surface is called with exactly what this was handed

`second_submission()` submits BOTH Jobs in ONE submission, each against its own input digest and Work
five configured workers: Job A's three, plus implementation-worker-b (its own real source, base and Work) and review-worker-b
